question.problem: Expressed as a decimal in its simplest form, $(-1.4)^{2}=${{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
We need to calculate the product of $(-1.4)$ with itself:

$$
(-1.4)^{2}=(-1.4)\cdot (-1.4)=(1.4)\cdot (1.4)
$$

First, we ignore the decimal points and multiply as if both numbers were whole numbers:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \begin{aligned} &  &  & \,\,\,\,\begin{aligned}\boxed{} \\ \boxed{1}\end{aligned}\,\,\,\, &  \\  &  &  & \,\,\,\,1\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,4\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,\,\times \,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,1\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,4\,\,\,\, \\  &  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,5\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,6\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,\,+\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,1\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,4\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,1\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,9\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,6\,\,\,\,\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $14\times 14=196.$

We now count the total number of decimal places in the two factors.

There is $1$ decimal place in the first factor ($1.4$) and $1$ decimal place in the second factor ($1.4$), so their product will have $1+1=2$ decimal places.

We take our value of $196$ and insert a decimal point to make a number with $2$ decimal places:

$$
1\,\overset{↓}{.}\,\,\,{{96}_{⏟}}_{2\text{ digits}}
$$

Therefore, $(-1.4)^{2}=1.96\,.$
